# Content Engine

Curated by Skill Harbor: a content-production skill that builds platform-native content without flattening the author's real voice into platform slop. It starts from source material (articles, notes, demos, docs, transcripts, screenshots, prior posts), adapts the format per platform (X opens with the strongest claim, LinkedIn expands only enough for outsiders to follow, short video scripts around the visual sequence, YouTube shows the tension early, newsletters open with the point), and enforces non-negotiables: one post carries one actual claim, specificity beats adjectives, no engagement bait unless asked. The repurposing flow extracts 3 to 7 atomic claims from one anchor asset, ranks them by sharpness and proof, and assigns one strong idea per output, and a quality gate checks that every draft sounds like the intended author and contains a real claim. It treats brand-voice (also in this batch) as the canonical voice layer: run it first when voice consistency matters across outputs. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it needs real source material to work from, generic post formulas are explicitly banned so "just write me something viral" will get you a request for sources instead; it drafts, it does not publish for you. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
